name: Laureate Education, Inc.
reason: Mexico/Peru for-profit universities with EBIT margin at a 10y high of 25.3% after years of divestitures (revenue CAGR -8.8%) and EPS still only 0.41x its 10y max; FX, emerging-market politics and education regulation make a 10-year forecast unreliable.

name: Legence Corp.
reason: 2025 IPO roll-up of HVAC/MEP contractors with negative GAAP EPS (-$0.57), 3.6% EBIT margin, acquisitions at 1.05x FCF and 3.5x net debt/EBITDA; the 9.2% FCF yield is new and unproven for a construction-services business with no demonstrated moat.

name: Labcorp Holdings Inc.
reason: Durable lab-testing duopoly with DGX, but EBIT margin has fallen from 21% to 10.9% (27th pctile), EPS -4.4%/yr over 5y, adjusted EPS runs 66% above GAAP and Medicare/PAMA reimbursement plus acquisitions (0.57x FCF) cloud the earnings path.

name: L3Harris Technologies Inc
reason: Growth built by mergers (Harris/L3, Aerojet; shares +5.8%/yr over 10y) rather than the core, EBIT margin down from 19% to 10.7%, adjusted EPS 72% above GAAP and a single US-government customer; FCF yield of 7% does not make it special.

name: Liberty Latin America Ltd.
reason: Levered Caribbean/LatAm telecom (4.9x net debt/EBITDA) with GAAP losses every year since 2017, negative 10y ROIC and acquisitions at 2.2x FCF; the 14% FCF yield is leverage-funded equity, not a special business.

name: Lineage, Inc.
reason: Recently IPO'd cold-storage REIT with negative GAAP EPS every year, EBIT margin down to 4.7%, 7.0x net debt/EBITDA and AFFO falling with industry oversupply; too levered and unproven.

name: Lockheed Martin Corporation
reason: High-ROIC (27.6% 10y avg) defense prime with shrinking share count, but EPS has fallen 2.6%/yr over 5y on large fixed-price/classified program charges, margin at 18th pctile (9.9%) and all revenue rests on US/allied defense budgets - program-level outcomes are not forecastable.

name: Cheniere Energy, Inc.
reason: LNG exporter whose earnings swing with global gas/LNG spreads (EPS $40.72 in 2023 vs $14.20 in 2024, 2020-21 losses) and consensus FY1 EPS -56%; commodity-set earnings with 3.4x net debt/EBITDA.

name: Lantheus Holdings Inc
reason: Radiopharma earnings concentrated in Pylarify (PSMA PET) and Definity, facing new PSMA-agent competition and pricing pressure; EBIT margin already down from 38% to 20%, adjusted EPS 282% above GAAP and shares +10.8%/yr - a credible product/competition threat within 5 years.

name: Lowe's Companies, Inc.
reason: Home-improvement duopoly with HD, 10y EPS CAGR 14.1% driven by margin gains (8.4% to 11.8%) and 4.9%/yr share shrink, 23.9% 10y ROIC; EPS 0.9x its 2022 peak in a depressed housing-turnover market gives a plausible 7-9% route, though 3.5x net debt/EBITDA (buyback-funded) needs watching.

name: Liquidia Corporation
reason: Single-product PAH biotech (Yutrepia) just reaching commercial launch with losses every year (EPS -$0.80 in 2025), negative FCF and ongoing patent litigation with United Therapeutics - binary outcome.

name: Lucky Strike Entertainment Corporation
reason: Bowling/entertainment venues with 11.2x net debt/EBITDA, GAAP losses in most years and NTM P/E of 394x; FCF yield of 9% rests on a highly levered discretionary business that could not comfortably survive a recession.

name: Lumen Technologies, Inc.
reason: Secularly declining legacy telecom (revenue -3.6%/yr over 10y, EBIT margin -1.5%), 7.0x net debt/EBITDA and GAAP losses; the 19% FCF yield reflects one-off AI fiber deal prepayments and asset sales rather than recurring cash.

name: Lamb Weston Holdings, Inc.
reason: Frozen-fry processor in an industry capacity glut with EBIT margin at a 9th-pctile 10.2% (from 17.9%), EPS 0.59x its 2023 peak, potato-crop/commodity cost exposure, low 0.47 FCF conversion and 3.7x net debt/EBITDA; activist-driven turnaround, not a forecastable compounder.

name: Lyft, Inc.
reason: Number-two US rideshare platform with negative GAAP EBIT margin (-2.6%), adjusted EPS far above GAAP (2025 EPS boosted by one-offs) and FCF flattered by stock comp; autonomous-vehicle disintermediation is a credible 5-year threat.

name: Mid-America Apartment Communities, Inc.
reason: Well-run Sunbelt apartment REIT, but FFO/share grew only 4.7%/yr over 10y with shares +4.5%/yr, FFO 0.93x its 2023 peak with consensus falling on new supply, and 4.3x net debt/EBITDA - no route to 7%+ per-share growth.

name: Macerich Company
reason: Regional-mall REIT with FFO/share down 9.3%/yr over 10y (1.43 vs 3.81), 9.1x net debt/EBITDA and dilutive equity issuance (shares +4.9%/yr); structurally challenged and over-levered.

name: Masco Corporation
reason: Good brands (Delta, Behr) and 24% ROIC, but revenue grew only 0.6%/yr over 10y with EPS growth coming from buybacks, EPS at 0.97x its 10y peak in a housing-repair cycle and Behr's heavy dependence on Home Depot - good but not special.

name: MasterBrand Inc
reason: Housing-cyclical cabinet maker with GAAP EPS down 78% in 2025 to $0.21, EBIT margin at 14th pctile (4.8%), 4.4x net debt/EBITDA after the Supreme acquisition; the 14% FCF yield is cyclical working-capital-aided cash from a commoditized product.

name: McDonald's Corporation
reason: Asset-light franchisor/landlord with 46% EBIT margin, 10y EPS CAGR 9.4% (5y 15.1%) and shares -2.7%/yr; EPS and margin at 10y highs but this is a non-cyclical royalty-and-rent stream, 3.7x net debt/EBITDA is fine for a defensive, and unit growth plus buybacks give a plausible ~7-8% route (watch GLP-1 and low-income traffic).
